guides.title: Phone will not charge: safe first checks
safety: Do not insert metal objects into the charging port.
Stop if the phone or battery is swollen, hot, leaking, or smells unusual.
guides.sourceTitle: Apple Support — If your iPhone or iPod touch won’t charge

steps.title: Check the power source
steps.body: Try a known-working wall outlet and compatible charging adapter. Test the outlet with another device.

steps.title: Inspect the cable and adapter
steps.body: Look for fraying, bent connectors, scorch marks, or looseness. Stop using damaged accessories.

steps.title: Inspect the port without probing it
steps.body: Use a flashlight to look for visible debris. Do not use pins, liquids, or metal tools. If packed debris is present, follow manufacturer service guidance or ask a repair professional.

steps.title: Restart and test again
steps.body: Restart the phone, connect the known-working charger, and allow a few minutes. If it still fails, the port, battery, or charging circuit may need professional diagnosis.

guides.title: Phone battery drains quickly
safety: Power the device off before external inspection.
Do not open sealed batteries or mains-powered equipment.
Stop if you notice swelling, smoke, burning smells, liquid damage, or excessive heat.

steps.title: Check battery usage
steps.body: Open battery settings and identify apps using an unusually large share of power.

steps.title: Review background activity
steps.body: Close apps you do not need and restrict background refresh for apps where appropriate.

steps.title: Check signal and display settings
steps.body: Weak mobile signal and very high brightness can increase battery use. Test with moderate brightness and a stable connection.

steps.title: Retest safely
steps.body: Restart and monitor battery use. If the phone heats up, swells, or drains suddenly after normal checks, seek service.

guides.title: Phone feels unusually hot
safety: Power the device off before external inspection.
Do not open sealed batteries or mains-powered equipment.
Stop if you notice swelling, smoke, burning smells, liquid damage, or excessive heat.

steps.title: Stop heavy activity
steps.body: Pause games, navigation, video recording, or other intensive tasks.

steps.title: Disconnect accessories
steps.body: Unplug the charger and accessories if safe. Move the phone out of direct sunlight.

steps.title: Let it cool naturally
steps.body: Place it on a dry, ventilated surface. Do not put it in a refrigerator or use ice.

steps.title: Check for warning signs
steps.body: If it remains very hot, smells unusual, or the battery swells, stop using it and arrange professional service.

guides.title: Phone will not turn on
safety: Power the device off before external inspection.
Do not open sealed batteries or mains-powered equipment.
Stop if you notice swelling, smoke, burning smells, liquid damage, or excessive heat.

steps.title: Check for visible damage
steps.body: Look for liquid exposure, cracks, swelling, or a damaged charging port. Stop if battery damage is suspected.

steps.title: Charge with compatible accessories
steps.body: Try a known-working compatible cable and adapter for a short period.

steps.title: Try the model-specific restart
steps.body: Use the manufacturer's instructions for the exact model; button combinations differ.

steps.title: Escalate if it stays blank
steps.body: If there is no response, avoid opening the phone. The battery, display, or power circuitry may need diagnosis.

guides.title: Phone cannot connect to Wi-Fi
safety: Power the device off before external inspection.
Do not open sealed batteries or mains-powered equipment.
Stop if you notice swelling, smoke, burning smells, liquid damage, or excessive heat.

steps.title: Check the network
steps.body: Confirm another device can connect to the same Wi-Fi network.

steps.title: Toggle Wi-Fi
steps.body: Turn Wi-Fi off and on, then select the correct network and re-enter its password if required.

steps.title: Restart network equipment
steps.body: If other devices also fail, restart the router according to its manual.

steps.title: Forget only if needed
steps.body: Forget and rejoin the network if you know the password. Avoid factory reset as an early troubleshooting step.

guides.title: Phone speaker has no sound
safety: Power the device off before external inspection.
Do not open sealed batteries or mains-powered equipment.
Stop if you notice swelling, smoke, burning smells, liquid damage, or excessive heat.

steps.title: Check sound settings
steps.body: Raise media volume, check silent mode, and make sure audio is not routed to Bluetooth headphones.

steps.title: Test different audio
steps.body: Try a ringtone, a local video, and a call speaker to narrow down the symptom.

steps.title: Inspect external openings
steps.body: Check for visible blockage and clean only the exterior with a dry, soft cloth. Do not insert objects.

steps.title: Retest and seek help
steps.body: If sound remains absent or distorted after a restart, a speaker or audio component may need service.

guides.title: Phone camera looks blurry or will not open
safety: Power the device off before external inspection.
Do not open sealed batteries or mains-powered equipment.
Stop if you notice swelling, smoke, burning smells, liquid damage, or excessive heat.

steps.title: Clean the lens gently
steps.body: Use a clean microfiber cloth and remove any case or lens accessory that could obstruct the camera.

steps.title: Check the selected camera
steps.body: Switch between front and rear cameras and test another app that uses the camera.

steps.title: Restart and check updates
steps.body: Close the camera app, restart the phone, and install official updates when convenient.

steps.title: Avoid internal cleaning
steps.body: If the lens is cracked, fogged internally, or the app repeatedly crashes, use authorized repair guidance.

guides.title: Laptop overheating: airflow checks
safety: Power the device off before external inspection.
Do not open sealed batteries or mains-powered equipment.
Stop if you notice swelling, smoke, burning smells, liquid damage, or excessive heat.

steps.title: Save work and check the surface
steps.body: Save your work. Place the laptop on a hard, flat surface; avoid beds, blankets, and cushions that block vents.

steps.title: Check ventilation openings
steps.body: Shut down and unplug the laptop, then visually check that external vents are not covered.

steps.title: Close unnecessary applications
steps.body: Restart and use Task Manager or Activity Monitor to identify unusually heavy CPU use.

steps.title: Retest and escalate
steps.body: Monitor temperature and fan noise. Persistent overheating may require model-specific service.

guides.title: Laptop is running slowly
safety: Power the device off before external inspection.
Do not open sealed batteries or mains-powered equipment.
Stop if you notice swelling, smoke, burning smells, liquid damage, or excessive heat.

steps.title: Restart the computer
steps.body: Save open work and restart rather than only closing the lid.

steps.title: Check resource usage
steps.body: Use Task Manager or Activity Monitor to identify apps consuming unusually high CPU or memory.

steps.title: Free up storage carefully
steps.body: Use the operating system's storage tool to remove temporary files; do not delete files you do not recognize.

steps.title: Check updates and security
steps.body: Install official system updates and run the built-in security scan. Persistent slowness may need diagnosis.

guides.title: Laptop battery drains quickly
safety: Power the device off before external inspection.
Do not open sealed batteries or mains-powered equipment.
Stop if you notice swelling, smoke, burning smells, liquid damage, or excessive heat.

steps.title: Review battery usage
steps.body: Open system battery settings and check which apps consume the most energy.

steps.title: Reduce avoidable load
steps.body: Lower screen brightness and close unused apps or external devices.

steps.title: Check power mode
steps.body: Choose a balanced or energy-saving mode when appropriate.

steps.title: Review battery health
steps.body: Use the manufacturer's battery-health utility. A worn battery may need replacement by a qualified provider.

guides.title: Laptop keyboard keys are not responding
safety: Power the device off before external inspection.
Do not open sealed batteries or mains-powered equipment.
Stop if you notice swelling, smoke, burning smells, liquid damage, or excessive heat.

steps.title: Check whether the issue is app-specific
steps.body: Try typing in another application and confirm the correct input language.

steps.title: Restart and check settings
steps.body: Restart the laptop and review accessibility settings such as Filter Keys.

steps.title: Inspect the surface
steps.body: Shut down and unplug. Remove loose debris only from the surface; do not pour liquid or spray cleaner into the keyboard.

steps.title: Test an external keyboard
steps.body: If an external keyboard works but built-in keys do not, model-specific service may be needed.

guides.title: Laptop turns on but screen stays black
safety: Power the device off before external inspection.
Do not open sealed batteries or mains-powered equipment.
Stop if you notice swelling, smoke, burning smells, liquid damage, or excessive heat.

steps.title: Check power indicators
steps.body: Connect the correct adapter and look for power or charging indicators.

steps.title: Adjust brightness and display mode
steps.body: Increase brightness and disconnect external displays or docks if attached.

steps.title: Try a normal restart
steps.body: Hold the power button only as directed by the manufacturer, noting that unsaved work may be lost.

steps.title: Avoid opening the display
steps.body: If the screen remains blank, the display, memory, or graphics system may need professional diagnosis.

guides.title: Headphones have no sound: basic checks
safety: Power the device off before external inspection.
Do not open sealed batteries or mains-powered equipment.
Stop if you notice swelling, smoke, burning smells, liquid damage, or excessive heat.

steps.title: Check volume and output
steps.body: Raise device volume, check mute, and confirm the headphones are selected as the audio output.

steps.title: Reconnect the headphones
steps.body: For Bluetooth models, disconnect and reconnect. For wired models, reseat the plug gently.

steps.title: Check charge and pairing
steps.body: Charge wireless headphones and follow the manufacturer's pairing instructions.

guides.title: Only one headphone side works
safety: Power the device off before external inspection.
Do not open sealed batteries or mains-powered equipment.
Stop if you notice swelling, smoke, burning smells, liquid damage, or excessive heat.

steps.title: Check audio balance
steps.body: Review left-right audio balance and mono-audio settings on the connected device.

steps.title: Reconnect or reseat
steps.body: Reconnect Bluetooth headphones or gently reseat a wired plug.

steps.title: Test another device
steps.body: Connect to another compatible device to see whether the problem follows the headphones.

steps.title: Avoid dismantling sealed units
steps.body: If one side remains silent, internal wiring or driver damage may need service.

guides.title: Bluetooth headphones will not pair
safety: Power the device off before external inspection.
Do not open sealed batteries or mains-powered equipment.
Stop if you notice swelling, smoke, burning smells, liquid damage, or excessive heat.

steps.title: Charge the headphones
steps.body: Make sure the headphones have enough charge and are in pairing mode as described in their manual.

steps.title: Check Bluetooth settings
steps.body: Enable Bluetooth and select the correct device name.

steps.title: Clear stale pairing carefully
steps.body: Remove the old pairing entry only if you can put the headphones back into pairing mode.

steps.title: Check another device
steps.body: Test with another compatible device. If pairing still fails, consult the manufacturer's reset procedure.

guides.title: Controller stick drift or movement
safety: Power the device off before external inspection.
Do not open sealed batteries or mains-powered equipment.
Stop if you notice swelling, smoke, burning smells, liquid damage, or excessive heat.

steps.title: Check the game settings
steps.body: Test in another game or the platform's controller test to rule out in-game dead-zone settings.

steps.title: Reconnect the controller
steps.body: Disconnect and reconnect it, or restart the console or computer.

steps.title: Update controller software
steps.body: Install firmware updates from the console or controller manufacturer.

steps.title: Do not force the stick
steps.body: Avoid liquids and disassembly. Persistent drift may require manufacturer service or replacement.

guides.title: Controller buttons do not respond
safety: Power the device off before external inspection.
Do not open sealed batteries or mains-powered equipment.
Stop if you notice swelling, smoke, burning smells, liquid damage, or excessive heat.

steps.title: Check the game and mapping
steps.body: Test another game and confirm button mapping or accessibility settings.

steps.title: Reconnect and recharge
steps.body: Use a known-good compatible cable or charge the controller.

steps.title: Clean only the exterior
steps.body: Power off and wipe the surface with a dry cloth. Do not pour liquids around buttons.

steps.title: Retest
steps.body: If a button remains stuck or unresponsive, avoid forcing it and seek model-specific service.

guides.title: Controller disconnects repeatedly
safety: Power the device off before external inspection.
Do not open sealed batteries or mains-powered equipment.
Stop if you notice swelling, smoke, burning smells, liquid damage, or excessive heat.

steps.title: Check battery level
steps.body: Charge the controller and inspect the cable if using a wired connection.

steps.title: Reduce wireless interference
steps.body: Move closer to the console or computer and temporarily disconnect unnecessary wireless accessories.

steps.title: Reconnect using official steps
steps.body: Follow the manufacturer's pairing instructions for the exact model.

steps.title: Update and retest
steps.body: Check official firmware updates. Persistent disconnections may indicate hardware or radio issues.

guides.title: Gadget will not turn on: safe first checks
safety: Power the device off before external inspection.
Do not open sealed batteries or mains-powered equipment.
Stop if you notice swelling, smoke, burning smells, liquid damage, or excessive heat.

steps.title: Identify the exact model
steps.body: Find the model number and locate the manufacturer's manual.

steps.title: Check power safely
steps.body: Confirm the outlet works and use only a compatible, undamaged adapter.

steps.title: Look for visible damage
steps.body: Check the exterior for cracks, liquid, heat damage, or a loose connector.

steps.title: Stop if unsafe
steps.body: Do not open mains-powered equipment or battery packs. Seek qualified service if the issue persists.

guides.title: Gadget will not connect to another device
safety: Power the device off before external inspection.
Do not open sealed batteries or mains-powered equipment.
Stop if you notice swelling, smoke, burning smells, liquid damage, or excessive heat.

steps.title: Confirm compatibility
steps.body: Check the manual to confirm the devices support the same connection method.

steps.title: Restart both devices
steps.body: Power-cycle both devices following their manuals.

steps.title: Check cable or pairing
steps.body: Use a compatible, undamaged cable or follow the official wireless pairing steps.

steps.title: Retest and escalate
steps.body: Test with another compatible device if available. Avoid unofficial firmware or unknown utilities.

guides.title: Accessory cable appears damaged
safety: Do not use cables with exposed conductors, scorch marks, or damaged plugs.
Never handle damaged mains cables while connected to power.

steps.title: Disconnect it
steps.body: Stop using the cable if insulation is split, wires are exposed, connectors are bent, or scorch marks appear.

steps.title: Do not patch exposed wiring
steps.body: Do not tape over exposed conductors or continue using a cable that heats up.

steps.title: Use a compatible replacement
steps.body: Choose an accessory that meets the device manufacturer's specifications.

steps.title: Check the device port
steps.body: If the replacement also fails, stop testing and arrange service for the device.
